question:
In the figure, \(CD,\) \(AE,\) and \(BF\) are one-third of their respective sides. It follows that \(AN_2:N_2N_1:N_1D=3:3:1,\) and similarly for lines \(BE\) and \(CF.\) Then the area of triangle \(N_1N_2N_3\) is:

[Figure 1](figures/1952_AMC_12_Q49_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The supplied \(3:3:1\) divisions let us compare areas without finding any angles or side lengths. Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\), and let \(K=[ABC]>0\). Triangles with bases on the same line and a common opposite vertex have the same altitude, so their areas are proportional to their bases.

Since \(CD=\tfrac13BC\), we have \(BD=\tfrac23BC\), giving \([ABD]=\tfrac23K\). Also, the given division of \(AD\) gives
\[
\frac{AN_2}{AD}=\frac{3}{3+3+1}=\frac37.
\]
Using bases \(AN_2\) and \(AD\), with common opposite vertex \(B\), we obtain
\[
[ABN_2]=\frac37[ABD]
=\frac37\cdot\frac23K=\frac27K.
\]
The analogous divisions along \(BE\) and \(CF\) give \(BN_3/BE=3/7\) and \(CN_1/CF=3/7\). Since \(CE=\tfrac23CA\) and \(AF=\tfrac23AB\), the same shared-altitude reasoning gives
\[
[BCN_3]=\frac37[BCE]=\frac27K,
\]
\[
[CAN_1]=\frac37[CAF]=\frac27K.
\]
The three triangles \(ABN_2\), \(BCN_3\), and \(CAN_1\), together with the central triangle \(N_1N_2N_3\), fill \(ABC\). Their interiors do not overlap: the drawn segments \(AD\), \(BE\), and \(CF\) separate these regions. Therefore
\[
[N_1N_2N_3]
=K-3\left(\frac27K\right)
=\frac17K.
\]
The central triangle has \(\boxed{\tfrac17}\) of the area of \(ABC\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
